lead_time_analysis.stability: Highly Variable (bimodal: ~1 day and ~2.7–3 day clusters)

safety_lead_time.comparison_action: Reduce SAP safety lead time from 5.0 to 1.67 days; replace with explicit safety stock of 22,093 units

narrative: Material PL2__M058116F exhibits moderate demand variability (CV=0.29) after an initial ramp-up phase, with mean daily demand of ~13,200 units. Lead times are highly variable (CV=0.56) with a bimodal distribution suggesting two supplier delivery modes, making explicit safety stock essential. The recommended (r,Q) EOQ policy consolidates 124 annual replenishments into 23 large orders of 143,136 units, reducing total cost by 58.5% while introducing a 22,093-unit safety stock to achieve the 95% service level. Capacity utilization reaches 77.6%, well within the 212,835-unit storage limit.

research_insights.selected_model: (r, Q) Continuous-Review with EOQ order quantity
research_insights.selection_rationale: Steady-state demand with moderate CV and continuous consumption suits a fixed-order-quantity reorder-point model. The EOQ (143,136) substantially exceeds the MOQ (26,604), so the economic quantity is unconstrained and dominates the policy decision. High lead-time variability is absorbed by the sigma-LTD safety stock rather than a lead-time proxy.
research_insights.boundary_risk: No capacity constraint binds. Post-replenishment max inventory (165,229) is 77.6% of the 212,835-unit limit, leaving a 47,606-unit buffer.
